analysis: Examined the add-on hold ('busy') plumbing across three files. (1) CoordinatorClientState.swift: adds a lock-protected `_busy: ProviderBusy?` to ProviderState (lines 214, 307-314), accessed through the same OSAllocatedUnfairLock as the other state. No new concurrency hazard and no data exposure beyond a closed busy descriptor. (2) ModelAutopilotBusyReason.swift: adds an `addonHold` enum case (lines 11-13) in the closed vocabulary. Because the enum is CaseIterable and declaration order is report order, inserting it after shuttingDown changes the report ordering. This is a protocol-vocabulary change only. Whether the coordinator or consumers reject an unknown busy_reason string is outside the supplied evidence. (3) Messages.swift: adds an optional `busy` field to Register and Heartbeat, and wire keys busy_reason, busy_since_ms, busy_addon. Encode and decode go through Self.encodeBusy and Self.decodeBusy (call sites at head lines 1070, 1097, 1345, 1371). Their implementations are not in the supplied excerpt (the patch is truncated), so I could not inspect them. The new fields are provider-self-reported and only say the provider is refusing work. A malicious provider (ADV-001) can already withhold service, and these fields can only reduce routing eligibility. They do not grant authorization, change App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053), or touch prompt data, encryption, or attestation. The `busy_addon` string is an add-on identifier; a provider-controlled string could be a log-injection or size concern for the coordinator, but that is coordinator-owned and out of scope here. Open questions for integration: the encodeBusy/decodeBusy bodies (field bounds, sanitization of busy_addon), and whether the add-on hold actually closes admission and unloads models as the comment claims (the ProviderLoop code is not in this batch). T-041 and the prefix cache are not touched. No regressions identified in the supplied evidence.
